scope: Magnetic spin-wave pulse spreading, zero dispersion, caustic beams, higher-order dispersion, and experimental relevance to the current separable cosine one-magnon model.

papers.title: Dispersionless propagation of ultra-short spin-wave pulses in ultrathin yttrium iron garnet waveguides
evidence_locations: PDF pp. 6-7 and Fig. 2: measured temporal pulse widths and group velocity
PDF pp. 8-11 and Fig. 4: dipolar-exchange competition, broad velocity minimum
PDF p. 10: 2.5 ns Gaussian excitation, simulation field 0.1 Oe
papers.finding: Experimentally measured near suppression of temporal broadening of approximately 2.5 ns pulses over 10 micrometers around 5.2 GHz. The explanation is a broad weak-variation region of group velocity produced by dipolar-exchange competition.
papers.comparison: Direct magnetic example of linear dispersion engineering for a pulse. It is a confined waveguide with realistic dipolar-exchange dispersion, not the two-dimensional nearest-neighbor cosine band or proof of permanent preservation in both spatial directions.
papers.verification: Current official arXiv metadata and relevant existing local full-text passages inspected.

papers.title: Generation of Spin-Wave Pulses by Inverse Design
evidence_locations: PDF p. 2, method and Eq. (1): backward linear propagation plus antenna transfer function
PDF pp. 3-4, Fig. 2 and Eqs. (2)-(3): chirped self-compressing Gaussian target and generation fidelity
papers.finding: Theory with micromagnetic validation designs antenna driving for specified spin-wave profiles; self-compressing and rectangular pulses are demonstrated within the linear regime.
papers.comparison: Initial phase or spectral design for pulse shaping is already an established magnetic-wave route. Targeting a shape at one selected time is not maintaining that shape at every propagation time.
papers.verification: Official APS and arXiv identity verified; official versioned PDF downloaded, parsed, and relevant method/results read.

papers.title: All-Angle Collimation for Spin Waves
evidence_locations: PDF pp. 1-2: flat isofrequency contours and their normals
PDF p. 2: small excitation for the linear regime
PDF pp. 3-4: monochromatic-beam limitation and patterned YIG all-angle collimation
papers.finding: Dispersion engineering of Co/Py interfaces and patterned YIG produces monochromatic spin-wave collimation; flat isofrequency contours align the group-velocity direction.
papers.comparison: The relevant curve curvature is the curvature of an equal-frequency contour, not Gaussian curvature of the energy graph. It does not establish two-dimensional finite-bandwidth packet preservation.
papers.verification: Official arXiv metadata checked; relevant full text read. Journal year 2015 differs from arXiv posting year 2017.

papers.title: Caustic spin wave beams in soft, thin films: properties and classification
papers.authors_short: A. Wartelle, F. Vilsmeier, T. Taniguchi, and C. H. Back
evidence_locations: Section II.A: explicitly linear thin-film dispersion and model limitations
Section II.B, Eq. (5): stationary group-velocity direction along the slowness curve
Section III.D, PDF pp. 12-13 and Fig. 13: higher-order caustic with quartic directional and apparent-wavelength variation
papers.finding: Classifies caustic spin-wave beams and identifies higher-order caustic points where the group-velocity direction is unusually insensitive to a range of wavevectors; includes time-resolved Kerr microscopy validation of the broader framework.
papers.comparison: Higher-order flattening is known in magnetic systems, but the paper studies direction on a fixed-frequency curve. Its higher-order caustic is not identical to a vanishing full Hessian of the cosine energy graph.
papers.verification: Official arXiv metadata and HTML plus relevant local PDF passages inspected. The HTML rendering date was not treated as publication date.

papers.title: Shaping non-reciprocal caustic spin-wave beams
evidence_locations: PDF p. 2: caustic criterion on isofrequency curve
PDF p. 2, Eq. (1): susceptibility and excitation-field Fourier integral, explicitly steady-state magnetization
PDF pp. 3-5: simulation and BLS comparison
papers.finding: Nanoconstricted RF excitation and dipolar-exchange anisotropy shape non-reciprocal caustic-like spin-wave beams; a near-field model, micromagnetic simulations and BLS measurements are compared.
papers.comparison: A modern experimental route for selective spectral excitation and beam steering. It is a fixed-frequency driven response rather than freely evolving localized packets in the cosine model.
papers.verification: Official arXiv latest version verified as v4 revised 2026-02-11; DOI and journal record checked; relevant local full text read.

papers.title: Nonlinear suppression of dispersion broadening of ultrashort spin-wave pulses in thin YIG films
evidence_locations: PDF pp. 4-6: forward-volume geometry, 3 ns pulses, linear and nonlinear regimes
PDF pp. 6-8 and Figs. 2-3: 0.1 mW pulse broadening versus 1.5 mW compensation
PDF pp. 8-10: nonlinear threshold and damping
papers.finding: Experimentally, approximately 3 ns pulses broaden by about 2.2 times over 50 micrometers at low power, whereas higher power produces nonlinear compensation and nearly unchanged pulse width.
papers.comparison: This is a deliberately different mechanism: nonlinearity compensates nonzero dispersion. It is not a direct precedent for the linear single-magnon calculation, and its envelope-soliton terminology must not be applied to the current packets.
papers.verification: Official arXiv metadata and full PDF inspected; PDF downloaded and verified with signature, title and all-page text checks.

supplemental_leads.title: Non-linear spin dynamics in ferromagnetic films and Schrodinger's equation in the vicinity of the zero-dispersion point
supplemental_leads.status: Crossref metadata verified and saved. Publisher full text was inaccessible. An indexed reproduction of the original paper describes a third-order-dispersion nonlinear envelope equation near omega''=0; retain as a historical lead, not the sole scientific evidence.

supplemental_leads.title: Magnetically tunable Airy-like beam of magnetostatic surface spin waves
supplemental_leads.status: Official metadata and abstract verified; full text inaccessible. Abstract reports micromagnetic simulations using an imposed 3/2 phase pattern. Do not identify this designed Airy-like beam with spontaneous cubic deformation of a Gaussian packet.

supplemental_leads.title: Efficient geometrical control of spin waves in microscopic YIG waveguides
supplemental_leads.status: Current official arXiv metadata verified. Existing full text PDF pp. 7-8 reports weak frequency dependence of group velocity in the narrow end of a tapered guide; this is supporting dispersion-control evidence, not rigid propagation through the taper.

supplemental_leads.title: Dispersion-tunable low-loss implanted spin-wave waveguides for large magnonic networks
supplemental_leads.status: Official article text inspected for the device scope and Fig. 5. Ion implantation provides dispersion control and waveguide matching. Continuous-wave excitation and transmission are not a demonstration of zero-Hessian localized-packet propagation.
